Optimal.Notes: 40 Hz refresh with a 40 fps cap gives perfectly smooth, tear-free gameplay that ProtonDB reporters describe as 'smooth'. TDP capped at 11 W keeps temperatures and fan noise comfortable while leaving headroom for CPU burst during busy battles.

profiles.Summary: World of Tanks: HEAT runs well on the Steam Deck out of the box via Proton, with community reports noting smooth 90–110 fps at some settings and no significant tinkering required. The game's minimum PC GPU spec (GTX 1050 2 GB) is closely matched by the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, so low-to-medium settings with FSR upscaling are the sweet spot for stable, playable performance.
profiles.BasisNote: Profiles are based on ProtonDB community reports (trending Platinum, noting smooth out-of-box play at 90–110 fps with Proton) combined with the game's stated PC minimum spec matching the Deck's GPU class; specific in-game setting names are inferred from the genre and engine since no Deck-specific settings guide exists — verify option names on first launch and adjust shadow/effects quality first if frame rate is unstable.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and let Deck FSR upscale to 1280x800; combined with the in-game FSR Performance mode this keeps the GPU very light. 8 W TDP and a 40 Hz refresh rate (matching the 30 fps cap via 40 Hz / 1.33× pacing) minimise power draw for the longest sessions.

KnownIssues: No Linux-native build; runs through Proton (generally smooth, no major blockers reported)
Heavy gameplay load (large battles, lots of effects) may cause occasional frame dips per Steam store notes
60 GB storage requirement is large for Deck internal storage — microSD or SSD expansion recommended
In-App Purchases and online-only requirement mean a stable internet connection is mandatory

MaxPerformance.Notes: Community reports note 90–110 fps is achievable at some settings, so 60 fps at High is realistic for most scenes; GPU clock pinned to maximum and full 15 W TDP are needed to sustain it during heavy battles. Drop to Medium overall if frame rate dips below 50 in large engagements.
